title: Tanzanian Carrot and Pea Curry
community: Urban Tanzania — the colourful everyday vegetable curry
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Mchuzi wa Karoti na Mbaazi — carrots and peas in a spiced tomato curry. Colourful, sweet, and fast to make — the vegetable curry that children love most and that brings colour and sweetness to the Tanzanian table.
longDesc: Carrot and pea curry is the most child-friendly Tanzanian vegetable dish — the natural sweetness of the carrots and peas, the mild spicing, and the beautiful colour make it a favourite across all ages.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add carrots and water. Cover and cook 10 minutes until nearly tender.
chefTips: Carrots take longer than peas — add them first.
Fresh peas need 5 minutes; frozen only 2—3 minutes.
commonMistakes: Adding peas and carrots together — peas overcook.
cookingScience: The orange colour of carrots (beta-carotene) and the green of peas (chlorophyll) are preserved by brief cooking. Extended cooking converts chlorophyll to pheophytin — producing the dull grey-green of overcooked peas.
sustainabilityTips: Tanzania's highland regions produce excellent carrots and peas.
culturalNote: Carrot and pea curry is Tanzania's most colourful everyday vegetable dish — the vibrant orange and green that brightens every plate.
